title: Cap. IX Arg. 9 Sol: eternal non-election no more fights temporal creation than angelic passing-over fought angelic creation — greater difficulty with angels, seen intact
pass_a_gloss: We deny the consequence of the Major. For the eternal decree of God concerning certain men not to be elected, or to be reprobated, cannot fight more with their temporal creation than the passing-by or non-election of certain ones, constituted from eternity from the mere liberty of the Divine will, fought with the creation of the Angels. Nay, a greater difficulty seems in the cause of the Angels than of men; For men from eternity elected or passed by were represented unto the Divine mind as vitiated in a corrupt mass, and reprobable; but God looked upon the Angels intact in the same perfection in which he afterward founded them: If therefore the eternal reprobation of certain Angels sprung from the Divine good pleasure, and not from foresight of sin, by no means fought with their creation, no fight can rightly be conceived between the reprobation and creation of men, who are objected unto God reprobating as contaminated and slain by the sin of Adam.
pass_b_english: We deny the Major's consequence. God's eternal decree concerning certain men not to be elected, or to be reprobated, can no more fight their temporal creation than the passing-by or non-election of some angels — set from eternity by mere liberty of divine will — fought angelic creation. Indeed the difficulty seems greater with angels than with men. Men from eternity elect or passed by were shown to the divine mind as vitiated in a corrupt mass and reprobable; but God looked on the angels intact in the same perfection in which he later made them. So if eternal reprobation of certain angels sprung from divine good pleasure, not from foresight of sin, and in no way fought their creation, no fight can rightly be conceived between reprobation and creation of men, who are set before God reprobating as contaminated and slain by Adam's sin.
source_text: Negamus consequentiam Majoris. Nam aeternum Dei decretum de non-eligendis, sive reprobandis hominibus quibusdam non magis pugnare potest cum temporali eorundem creatione, quam cum Angelorum creatione pugnavit quorundam praeteritio sive non-electio, ex mera libertate voluntatis Divinae ab aeterno constituta. Imo major videtur difficultas in causa Angelorum quam hominum; Homines enim ab aeterno electi aut praeteriti repraesentabantur menti Divinae ut in massa corrupta vitiati, et reprobabiles; at Angelos integros Deus intuitus est in eadem perfectione, in qua eos postea condidit: Si igitur aeterna reprobatio quorundam Angelorum ex beneplacito Divino, et non ex peccati praevisione, orta minime pugnavit cum creatione eorundem, non potest recte concipi pugna ulla inter reprobationem et creationem hominum, qui Deo reprobanti objiciuntur, ut peccato Adae contaminati et occisi.
